findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Writes require explicit --apply and only occur when the healer finds a repair. The CLI accepts caller-selected roots and folders, so some external path use may be intentional.
findingDetails.claim: The default healer discovers a packet by the name spec.md without rejecting symlink entries, then opens the document and writes with fs.writeFileSync. With --apply, a repairable spec document symlink can therefore direct writes outside the packet and repository.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The anchor-repair and lane-mode paths use atomic replacement, which replaces a symlink instead of writing its referent. The default healer path is separate and uses fs.writeFileSync; no symlink rejection is present at discovery or before that write.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A realpath/lstat guard confines every default-healer document to the intended repository root, with a test showing an external symlink target remains unchanged under --apply.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject symlinked documents and verify the canonical document path remains under the selected repository root before reading or writing.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The default CLI reaches this write from discover(), and upgrade-legacy invokes the same healer with --apply for packet targets.
findingDetails.title: Default healer writes through symlinked packet documents

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Manifest generation records resource paths and does not read file contents. The risk arises when the generated manifest makes those paths available to consumers that follow the symlink.
findingDetails.claim: walkLeafFiles starts with references/assets or a declared scope path and immediately calls readdirSync on it. If that starting directory is a symlink to a directory outside the skill, readdirSync follows it; the per-entry symlink check never sees the root link, and external files are emitted as in-skill resource paths.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The walker resolves and confines symlink entries encountered below the starting directory, and lexical ../ scope traversal is rejected. The tests shown cover lexical traversal but do not create a symlinked starting scope.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: The walker canonicalizes and confines every starting scope before readdirSync, with tests for both default roots and declared directory scopes symlinked outside the skill.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve and validate each starting directory against the real skill root before walking it.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The same walkLeafFiles function handles default roots and scoped directories; collectScopedLeaves follows the starting path with statSync before invoking it.
findingDetails.title: Leaf walker follows a symlinked scope root outside the skill

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Normal archives use a directory inside the packet home, and the command is an explicit operator action. A malicious or accidental destination symlink changes the destination after the source check.
findingDetails.claim: archive_spec canonicalizes and confines the source packet but builds archive_root as parent/z_archive and uses it without resolving or checking it. If z_archive is a symlink outside specs, the command copies the packet there, renames it there, then removes the source packet.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The source packet is canonicalized and rejected if outside specs, and a test excludes symlinked tracks. Those checks do not canonicalize or reject the z_archive destination itself.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: The archive root is checked by realpath after creation and proven to remain below specs before any copy or source removal; add an outside-target symlink test.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject a symlinked archive root and confirm its canonical path is beneath specs before copying or deleting the source.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The destination is constructed once at archive.sh:276 and is used by cleanup, copy, rename and source removal without a destination containment check.
findingDetails.title: Archive destination symlink can move packets outside specs

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The workflow is intended for integration branches and the fine-grained token may be tightly scoped. The exact exposure depends on the pinned checkout action behavior and token permissions.
findingDetails.claim: The privileged workflow passes TRIGGER_INDEX_PUSH_TOKEN to actions/checkout but does not disable credential persistence. It then runs npm ci before generating or pushing output. With checkout credential persistence enabled by default, install scripts can read the stored credential and expose the ruleset-bypass token.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The workflow triggers only on pushes to main or skilled/** and workflow_dispatch, not pull_request. The repository install is lockfile-based, but it still executes package lifecycle scripts while the checkout credential is available.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Verify the pinned checkout action does not persist credentials, or prove the token is removed before npm lifecycle scripts and is restricted to non-sensitive index writes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Disable checkout credential persistence and provide a narrowly scoped push credential only to the final commit/push step.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The token is passed to checkout at line 34 and the next build step runs npm ci at line 46; no persist-credentials override appears in the checkout inputs.
findingDetails.title: Write token is available to dependency installation scripts

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The eight-word signature may intentionally approximate the prior seeder's output, and the operator can inspect the dry-run report before applying it. That signature is not unique to generated content.
findingDetails.claim: The cleanup transform can alter an authored trigger phrase when it happens to have eight normalized words and ends in a configured stop word.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The cleanup is opt-in through --apply and its report previews exact old/new phrase blocks. The integration test verifies cleanup of a restored template block. The inspected tests do not include a custom authored eight-word phrase that ends in a stop word.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the intended contract explicitly treats every matching eight-word phrase as generated seed residue and a documented safeguard prevents authored phrases from entering that class.
findingDetails.evidence: descriptionStopWordEdits selects every spec trigger phrase with exactly eight normalized words whose last word is in DESCRIPTION_STOP_WORDS. It does not establish that the phrase came from the earlier description seeder. planDocumentChange applies this trim to every spec list even when no template block was found, and runCleanup writes the planned result under --apply. A matching authored phrase is therefore lowercased, punctuation-stripped, shortened, or deleted.
findingDetails.recommendation: Restrict the trim to phrases that can be matched to a known prior generated seed, or require an explicit per-file selection. Add a regression case that preserves an authored eight-word phrase ending in a stop word.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The only guard in descriptionStopWordEdits is the eight-word/trailing-stop-word shape at template-phrase-cleanup.mjs:304-307. planDocumentChange calls the trim for kind=spec at :374-388, and runCleanup walks each document and writes the plan when apply is enabled at :456-515. This reaches arbitrary spec.md trigger_phrases entries, not only known prior seed output.
findingDetails.title: Phrase cleanup can rewrite authored eight-token spec triggers

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The generator may stage all four outputs atomically or fail before changing the index; either behavior would make this partial-write scenario unreachable. The generator implementation was outside the selected file list, so that possibility remains unverified.
findingDetails.claim: A nonzero retry-generation exit can be ignored, allowing a partial rebuild to pass the index-only check while an existing sidecar remains stale.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The workflow's later checks were inspected: --check reads the main index and the sidecar loop checks only file existence. The generator's output transaction and write order were not inspected.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the generator is shown to write all outputs atomically and to leave no partial sidecar state on every nonzero exit.
findingDetails.evidence: The retry shell sets -u and pipefail but not -e, invokes the generator without checking its exit status, then checks only the main index and verifies sidecars only by file existence. If the generator updates the index and then fails before refreshing an existing sidecar, the index-only check can pass and the old sidecar can remain in the branch.
findingDetails.recommendation: Fail the retry immediately when generation returns nonzero, and validate the contents or freshness of all four outputs before committing.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The workflow has a separate initial generator step and one retry invocation at line 138. That retry call is not guarded; the following --check is documented in the workflow as index-only, and the later loop checks only -f for each sidecar.
findingDetails.title: Retry ignores a failed generator before its index-only check

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: CI may have been checked after the closeout note, or SC-002 may have been intended as advisory, but no waiver or later receipt is recorded in the cited packet.
findingDetails.claim: Phase 019 is marked complete although its explicit success criterion says main CI after the push was not checked.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the acceptance push receipt and implementation summary; neither records the post-push CI result named in SC-002.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A receipt proves main was green after the push, or the packet records a superseding waiver and aligns completion metadata.
findingDetails.evidence: SC-002 requires main CI to be green after the push and records that it was not checked; the parent nevertheless marks phase 19 Complete, and the cited push receipt does not prove CI status.
findingDetails.recommendation: Verify the post-push CI result and record it, or explicitly waive/supersede SC-002 and align the phase completion state.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The success criterion, acceptance evidence, implementation summary and parent status are all present and make the missing CI receipt observable.
findingDetails.title: Phase 019 is complete while its post-push CI criterion is unverified

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The eight-token pattern originated from generated descriptions, so an authored phrase with the same shape may be uncommon, but the predicate cannot distinguish it.
findingDetails.claim: The cleanup transform can trim an authored trigger phrase solely because it has eight normalized words and ends in a configured stop word.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the seed/cleanup relationship and the integration test; the cleanup predicate does not record provenance, and the cited test does not protect an authored phrase matching the same shape.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Preserve provenance for generated phrases or add a regression test proving an authored matching phrase remains byte-identical under --apply.
findingDetails.evidence: The cleanup selects matching spec trigger phrases without proving they came from the description seeder, applies the edits to spec lists even when no template block was found, and writes the result under --apply.
findingDetails.recommendation: Limit the transform to phrases with known template provenance or preserve authored phrase text and test that boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The same cleanup predicate processes every spec trigger list and the write path persists its planned edits; no provenance check gates that path.
findingDetails.title: Phrase cleanup can rewrite authored eight-token spec triggers

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The skill may be written for interactive sessions, but the implementation command presents the ask-and-wait behavior as unconditional and does not gate it by runtime mode.
findingDetails.claim: The child-dispatch exemption in root instructions conflicts with unconditional spec-folder ask-and-wait rules in the skill and implementation command.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Compared the root child-dispatch exception with the canonical skill, Hermes mirror, and implementation command; none of the latter three expresses the exception.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Add an explicit non-interactive child-dispatch branch to the skill, mirror, and implementation contract, then verify the contracts remain aligned.
findingDetails.evidence: The root instructions pre-resolve Gate 3 for AI_SESSION_CHILD=1, while the skill and Hermes mirror require A/B/C/D on file modifications and the implementation YAML says to stop and wait.
findingDetails.recommendation: Make the child-dispatch pre-resolution explicit in each routed contract so unattended workers do not wait for an unavailable answer.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The root, canonical skill, Hermes mirror, and implementation YAML are the four cited rule surfaces; the same ask-and-wait requirement appears in the latter three.
findingDetails.title: Child-dispatch Gate 3 exception is missing from the skill and implementation command

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The generator may stage all outputs atomically or fail before changing the index, which would make the partial-write case unreachable; that behavior remains unverified.
findingDetails.claim: A nonzero retry-generation exit can be ignored, allowing a partial rebuild to pass the index-only check while an existing sidecar remains stale.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The later --check verifies the index only and the sidecar loop verifies -f; the generator transaction and output write order were not in the assigned file set.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Show that generation is atomic and leaves no partial sidecar state on every nonzero exit.
findingDetails.evidence: The retry shell uses set -uo pipefail without -e, invokes the generator without checking its status, then checks only the main index and sidecar existence. A partial write can leave stale sidecar content.
findingDetails.recommendation: Fail immediately when retry generation returns nonzero and validate the contents or freshness of all four outputs before committing.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The retry invocation is unguarded, the following check is explicitly index-only, and the sidecar validation tests existence rather than content or freshness.
findingDetails.title: Retry ignores a failed generator before its index-only check

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The wrappers are short and may intentionally keep selection logic local because they serve different repair surfaces.
findingDetails.claim: Three healer CLI entrypoints duplicate the same --folder, --roots, and default specs-root target selection.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the upgrade fold-in repeats the algorithms and whether the three wrappers need different target-selection rules; the helper paths are reused and the option resolution is repeated.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the entrypoints are intentionally independent and tests pin their selection parity, retain this as an optional duplication advisory.
findingDetails.evidence: runAnchorRepair, runLaneModesCli, and main each resolve the same folder/root options; upgrade-legacy reuses exported repair helpers rather than repeating those algorithms.
findingDetails.recommendation: Consider a shared target-selection helper if these entrypoints need future behavioral changes, with parity tests for their options.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Only the three CLI wrappers repeat target selection; the upgrade caller delegates to shared helpers.
findingDetails.title: Healer CLI target selection is duplicated across three entrypoints

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The catalog may assume the report is run only in a recognized repository layout, but the CLI classifier explicitly has an unknown result for neither root.
findingDetails.claim: The catalog says a repository with no specs folder reads as v3, while the classifier returns unknown when neither the v4 nor legacy root exists.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Compared the catalog sentence with the root-detection conditions and an existing test for legacy-root classification; the test does not cover a repository with neither root.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Clarify that the catalog sentence assumes a legacy root, or add a no-roots case proving the documented classification.
findingDetails.evidence: The classifier sets v3 from a legacy root or description residue and returns unknown when both v3 and v4 are false; the catalog sentence says no specs folder means v3.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct the catalog wording to describe the unknown no-roots case or state its layout precondition.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The feature-catalog statement and classifier return are direct counterparts; the classifier has a distinct unknown branch when neither root is present.
findingDetails.title: Repository-era catalog overstates the no-specs case
